token_budget_review.metadata: runtime.latest_call_tool forwards its fourth and fifth arguments as arguments and meta to latest_connections.call_tool. The stdio thread_hint schema is an empty object with additionalProperties=false and its handler reads context.meta['threadId']. Passing {} plus canonical threadId metadata corrects the observed missing-hint path.
token_budget_review.guard_retention: The HeptaGovernance and active-tool-policy no-call guards, token-budget/context-window gates, environment=None, no-wait/default-timeout arguments, latest connection route, .ok() error handling, content extraction and context rendering remain byte-identical outside the three-line argument move/comment.
token_budget_review.finish_owner: The private helper waits only after TurnComplete, passes that completed.turn_id to the existing observer and awaits its returned future after all registry locks are released. The observer filters TaskTerminalizationKind::Finish plus exact owner turn ID; it neither claims nor retires owners. The task publishes TurnComplete before persistence, marker release, pending work and finish completion. Both parameterized cases use this helper immediately before the next submit_turn.
token_budget_review.coverage_retained: All existing compaction lifecycle, request count, window lineage, hidden-tool exposure, developer context and regex assertions remain unchanged. No deadline, feature, policy, production terminalizer, or retry changes.
token_budget_review.limits: The closed compaction failures contain the generic ten-second event timeout, not a per-owner scheduling trace. The omitted finish observation is a source-proven reachable interleaving; native success remains unmeasured.

turn_state_review.identity: The original test's metadata assertions distinguish read-only prewarm from danger-full-access sampling; unchanged submit_turn explicitly selects PermissionProfile::Disabled. The exact source compatibility projection removes the prewarm phase and volatile turn lineage but retains sandbox and sandbox_mode, and WebsocketConnectionIdentity compares the serialized projection. The fixture must admit the resulting new connection.
turn_state_review.fixture_liveness: The original server serially consumes one scripted connection before accepting another. Leaving the prewarm connection waiting for later sampling requests prevents accepting the identity-changing socket. Closing only the one-request prewarm script permits acceptance; the actual three-request sampling script remains open until explicit shutdown.
turn_state_review.within_turn: The second test's original three response batches remain byte-token identical and all execute on connection index 1. Exact [1,3] plus unchanged [null,ts-1,ts-1] assertions still reject sampling reconnections and later metadata overriding the first state. The added first batch supplies only the otherwise missing generate=false prewarm response.
turn_state_review.across_turns: The first test retains all four original response batches. Exact [1,3] proves first sampling, tool follow-up and next logical turn share the second physical connection. The original turn-state sequence, request_kind, generate, sandbox_mode and same/different turn-ID assertions remain unchanged after flattening the two connection logs.
turn_state_review.limits: Closing the prewarm script can itself force reconnection, so [1,3] alone does not prove that production compatibility identity requires it. That requirement is separately supported by the unchanged projection and permission-selection source. These tests retain same-turn and cross-turn sampling connection coverage; they do not independently qualify prewarm reuse under identical permissions.
